The story strikes an effective and natural balance between scene and summary/exposition. It uses exposition and summary at the beginning to establish the setting (the contrast between suburban Larchmont and urban Chelsea in the late 1990s) and the central conflict (the father's advanced stage of AIDS), as well as in the middle to compress the first few days of the cruise and show how Clara is adopted by the ship's community. It then transitions seamlessly into vivid, real-time scenes—such as the phone call with the mother, unpacking in the stateroom, meeting Mateo on the deck, and the emotional climax at the White Party—allowing the characters' relationships and emotional weight to unfold naturally through dialogue and action.
